method: Official primary documentation opened and relevant sections read using web tool; no OS qualification experiment

sources.supports: Scheduling interval bandwidth; nested CPU rates relative to parent; no cumulative lifetime termination contract
Periodic user-mode job/process limits; 100ns representation; cumulative job end limit based on existing consumption
Total user/kernel time includes active and terminated members; period counters have independent reset semantics
Retained process-handle user/kernel accounting summed across threads; represented by 100ns FILETIME values
Subtree resource aggregation and nested termination; limit semantics are resource-specific
Termination of associated processes and child jobs; not itself a complete AgentNexus ExitProof
External termination is asynchronous; pending I/O must complete/cancel; wait on retained process handle for exit
Process object signaling and retained-handle lifetime; process exit is not whole-tree evidence
Hierarchical controllers; cpu.max period bandwidth; cpu.stat user/system/usage accounting; cgroup.kill subtree; scheduler restrictions
Normal-scheduler quota replenishes each period; per-CPU slices and bandwidth throttling
Fuel/epoch instrumentation bounds guest execution units with stated trap accounting limits; not OS CPU milliseconds

inferences: No numeric worst-case supervisor or sampling stop latency is asserted without a documented and qualified bound for every stage.
Dividing an unbounded stage into admission steps does not prove the CPU bound of the currently running step.
cpu.max and cpu.stat followed by cgroup.kill do not establish the unchanged AgentNexus cumulative CPU overshoot contract.
Guest fuel is a distinct potential contract; no validated conversion to native user/kernel CPU milliseconds is available in this release.
